int_name: W SPENCER AVE & E WISTER ST

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and continuous sidewalks. However, the environment lacks advanced traffic calming measures or dedicated space for non-motorized transport beyond the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are showing signs of wear and fading, which may reduce their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the foreground and middle ground of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and increase visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Refresh the crosswalk markings using high-visibility, durable thermoplastic materials to ensure they are clearly visible to all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to provide a leading pedestrian interval, allowing pedestrians to enter the crosswalk before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The street environment provides a sidewalk on only one side of the roadway, with no formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure visible. Faded pavement markings and the presence of parked vehicles along the curb create potential visibility and safety issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded Pavement Markings
hazards.description: The transverse lines and lane markings are severely worn, making them nearly invisible to motorists.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved walkway, forcing pedestrians into the grass or the roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian crossing areas.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe walking path.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps with tactile paving, and a marked crosswalk. However, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded, and there is a lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals, which increases risk at this signalized crossing.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines are heavily worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible at the signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signal phases.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light pole on the left

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse markings with high-visibility continental (ladder) style markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way and crossing time information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with a faded zebra crosswalk and a traffic signal. The pedestrian environment is degraded by sidewalk obstructions such as trash bags and poorly maintained infrastructure adjacent to boarded-up buildings.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Large trash bags and debris are blocking the sidewalk, potentially forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: On the sidewalk to the left of the yellow building.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The zebra crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads, requiring pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic to improve driver awareness and compliance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve safety and clarity for crossing.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance and Clearance
interventions.description: Implement regular sanitation and maintenance to keep sidewalks clear of debris and in good repair.
